Manifesto/Zero-Bloat Delivery
Principle 03 / native web

Zero-Bloat Delivery

A small native surface improves portability, auditability, and courtside resilience.

Review deployment briefBack to Manifesto

Delivery

Why it matters

A rule for accountable court intelligence

The interface uses semantic HTML, layered CSS, and browser-native JavaScript. It can be served from a basic static host and remains usable without a framework runtime.

Zero dependency does not mean zero responsibility: browser support, security headers, accessibility, and content validation still require deployment testing.

A principle becomes a product claim only after representative human and technical validation.

Implementation rules

Operational guardrails

JavaScript

PWA

Verification evidence

How the principle is demonstrated

  1. Start from semantic content and working links.
  2. Add responsive layout from 320px upward.
  3. Enhance only where interaction adds value.
  4. Verify failure states and cache updates.
